stemBlocks.value: The quadratic function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 8x + 11. (a) Express f(x) in the form (x + h)² + k, where h and k are constants. (b) Hence state the coordinates of the minimum point of f. (c) Determine the equation of the axis of symmetry of the graph of f.
Think first: Halve the coefficient of x to find the number inside the bracket, then correct for what squaring the bracket adds.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p154-q01 from workbook page 154.

solutionSteps.instruction: Halve the coefficient of x to form the bracket.

contentBlocks.value: Half of -8 is -4, so start with (x − 4)²
(x − 4)² gives 16, but the function has 11, so subtract 5
(x − 4)² is never negative and equals 0 when x = 4, so the least value of f is -5
The vertical line through the vertex

strategyBlocks.value: Take half of -8 to build the bracket (x − 4)², subtract the extra 16 it introduces, then read the vertex and axis directly from the completed-square form.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) f(x) = (x − 4)² − 5, so h = -4 and k = -5  (b) Minimum point (4, -5)  (c) Axis of symmetry x = 4.

whyThisWorks.value: Completing the square rewrites a quadratic so the variable appears only once, inside a squared bracket. Since a square is never negative, the smallest possible value of (x − 4)² is 0, reached when x = 4, and the function's least value is then just the constant outside — here -5. The vertex and the axis of symmetry therefore fall straight out of the form with no further work.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to subtract the square of the halved coefficient, giving (x − 4)² + 11.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting to subtract the square of the halved coefficient, giving (x − 4)² + 11.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the minimum point as (-4, -5) — the bracket (x − 4)² is zero at x = +4.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the minimum point as (-4, -5) — the bracket (x − 4)² is zero at x = +4.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the axis of symmetry as y = 4 instead of x = 4.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the axis of symmetry as y = 4 instead of x = 4.
